name: warp_issue
kind: survey: declares cells, readings and how the readings decide between named alternatives; installs nothing
mechanisms: instruction issue (control word: stall, yield, dependency barriers)
why: dev/design/mechanism-recalibration.md: the issue model is re-derived from the smallest kernels with every instruction and control field chosen by hand. On the two smoke kernels the replay is already far from hardware on both devices (empty kernel: h100 508 cycles against 1209 replayed, b300 905 against 344; first-touch constant reads off by factors), and the hardware places its waits where the control word says (no barrier on sm_90a ULDC -> imc_miss at the load; write barrier on sm_103a LDCU / on LDC -> short_scoreboard at the reader).
data_seen_before_freezing: ptx_kernel smoke, both devices, one sampling pass each ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/ptx_kernel/{h100,b300}-smoke, -smoke2). First run: a barrier-writing load (LDC, sm_103a LDCU) with stall 1 followed at once by its reader gave wrong values (the reader used the stale register); with stall 2 the values are right. Second run, cycles per warp: empty kernel h100 no_instruction 357 on the first instruction, drain 190 after EXIT, b300 849 / 137; smoke kernel h100: first-touch ULDC lines 105-171 imc_miss at the load, a second word of a loaded line 0; reader of a first-touch bank-3 LDC 755 short_scoreboard; reader of LDC.64 on a line that ULDC had loaded 151; b300: nothing at the LDCU, readers 60-300, reader of the bank-3 LDC 703, first instruction 603.

ncu metric inventory of both devices (same directories, ncu/): per-SM instruction / constant cache request counters (h100 idc__requests*, b300 sm__icc_requests*, sm__dcc_requests*) and, b300 only, a per-GPC `L1.5` cache serving both instruction and constant requests in front of L2 (gcc__cache_requests_type_{instruction,constant}*, gcc__gcc2xbar_requests*). b300 has no imc_miss stall class.

Huerta et al., arXiv 2503.20481 (Ampere): source of hypotheses only (stall counter, yield, six dependency counters whose increment is visible one cycle after issue, separate constant caches for fixed-latency operands and for LDC, stream-buffer instruction prefetch).

probe.chain: tools/microbench/ptx_kernel (ptxas -O3 -> sass_patch free-mode plan -> nvdisasm gate -> ptx_runner). Generator tools/microbench/warp_issue/gen.py writes one plan per cell and architecture (probe/<cell>.<arch>.plan) and cells.tsv; the PTX sources (a frame of the needed size plus a donor of instruction forms) are regenerated at build time.
probe.sass_gate: the plan: the built function equals the plan line by line (text by nvdisasm, every control field of a body instruction given explicitly); a cell whose plan does not apply is recorded and not measured.
probe.framed_cell: prologue (per-thread output address), 2 NOPs with stall 8, clock, body, clock, three stores (clock, clock, R5), EXIT. R5 starts as the thread index; the body xors every loaded constant into it (or adds 1 per add); cells.tsv has the expected value.

families.a (start and exit): a.empty = stack load, EXIT. a.exit_only = EXIT. a.nop_exit = NOP, EXIT. a.stack_nop{16,64,256}_exit = stack load, n NOPs (stall 1), EXIT. Shapes of a.empty: one CTA; 1 / 8 / 32 warps per CTA on every SM; 4 and 16 CTAs of 8 warps per SM.
families.b (code fetch): b.sled.l{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128}: stack load, NOPs with stall 1 up to a whole number of 128 B lines, EXIT last.
families.c (constant reads): pairs = a load immediately followed by its reader (the load's stall is 2). c.{u,v}{0,3}.first8: eight first touches of eight 64 B lines through the uniform path (sm_90a ULDC, sm_103a LDCU) / the vector path (LDC), bank 0 (parameter blob) / bank 3. c.{u,v}0.reread: four first touches, then another word of the same four lines. c.u0.batch{4,8}, c.v0.batch4: n loads (stall 1), one NOP, their n readers. c.u0_then_v0 / c.v0_then_u0: four lines through one path, then another word of the same lines through the other path. c.{u,v}0.first8.head: the eight pairs are the kernel's first instructions after the stack load. c.u0.first8[.head].tail512: the same kernels with 512 never-executed NOP lines behind them in the function.
families.d (control word): d.nop.s<stall>.y<yield bit>: 64 NOPs with that stall and yield bit between the clocks (only combinations nvdisasm decodes: yield bit 1 with stall 1..11, yield bit 0 with any stall). d.add.s{1..4}: 64 in-place `VIADD R5, R5, 0x1` with that stall. d.visible.s{1,2}.g{0,1,2}: eight times [LDC with write barrier and stall s; g NOPs; reader waiting on the barrier].

probe.shapes: base: grid = SM count, 8 warps per CTA. Extra shapes per cells.tsv (1, 4, 32 warps per CTA on selected cells).

runner: tools/microbench/ptx_kernel/run_rows.sh per device: capture, two stall-sampling passes with the metric list tools/microbench/ptx_kernel/metrics.<device>.txt, replay with --stall-ledger (engine build recorded in the run directory). Rows: suites/<arch>/microbench set `warp_issue`. 4 launches per process, launch 0 measured. Output $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue/<device>. Values: the stored R5 of every thread of launch 0 against cells.tsv.

derivation.per_pc: cycles per warp per (pc, class) as cyclescope.stall.hardware scales them; executed counts per pc; clock difference per warp (median, min, max over warps) from the stored words.
derivation.counters: per launch: every metric of the list; for the cache counters requests / hits / misses per launched warp and per code line.
derivation.usable: sampling readings from rows with at least 2000 samples in both passes, values whose passes agree within 10 % or 5 cycles; counter and clock readings from every row.

questions_before_data.exit_drain: Alternative E1: the drain after EXIT is the completion of the warp's outstanding variable-latency instructions (here the stack LDC): then a.exit_only and a.nop_exit show under 20 cycles of drain and a.stack_nop256_exit shows under 20, while a.empty and a.stack_nop16_exit show a drain that shrinks by about the NOP time. E2: a fixed exit cost: all five within 20 % of each other. Anything else: reported.
questions_before_data.first_instruction: no_instruction cycles per warp on the first instruction of a.* and b.*: by warps per CTA (1, 8, 32), by CTAs per SM (1, 4, 16), on one CTA, with and without a stack load; next to the instruction-cache counters. F1 (cold code line fetched once per SM, shared by its warps): flat in warps per CTA, and with 16 CTAs per SM the mean falls because later CTAs find the line; F2 (a per-warp launch cost): flat in everything including 16 CTAs per SM. Reported with the counters; no threshold beyond `within 20 %` for flat.
questions_before_data.fetch: b.sled: no_instruction cycles per warp by code line (first pc of each 128 B line), kernel cycles and instruction-cache requests / misses against the number of lines. Reported: cycles per additional line (slope over l8..l128), the line indices that show a wait, counter requests per line.
questions_before_data.constants: per cell and load: wait at the load pc and at its reader pc, by class. Reported tables: first touch against re-read, bank 0 against bank 3, uniform against vector path, pairs against batch (C1 parallel service: the batch total is under 2 x the per-load first-touch time; C2 serial: over 0.75 x n x that time), the other-path cells (S1 shared resident set: the second path's loads cost within 10 cycles of a re-read; S2 separate: within 20 % of a first touch), head against late position, tail512 against none (T1: first-touch time changes by under 10 %; T2: reported with the size of the change), and by warps per CTA.
questions_before_data.stall: d.nop: clock difference per NOP against stall and yield bit, and the class of the samples on the NOP pcs. W1: per-NOP time = max(1, stall) within 0.1 cycle for yield bit 1 and the samples other than selected are `wait` (share at least 0.8 for stall >= 2). Otherwise the table is reported. By warps per CTA (1, 4, 8, 32): per-warp clock difference and not_selected share.
questions_before_data.fixed_latency: d.add: the smallest stall with the expected value in every thread, and the clock difference per add at each stall.
questions_before_data.barrier_visibility: d.visible: which (stall, gap) cells give the expected value in every thread. V1 (the increment is visible one cycle after issue): s1.g0 wrong, every other cell right.

install: Nothing is installed from this version. Each mechanism gets its own version with engine rules declared before its data, designed on these readings.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case.

addenda.when: h100 and b300 runs (70 cells each, two sampling passes, replay with engine build a45851a8; jobs ptxk-wi-{h100,b300}-{1,2}) — readings; nothing installed
addenda.text: Data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/warp_issue/{h100,b300}; tables by tools/microbench/warp_issue/derive.py. All 70 cells per device built (0 unrealised), captured, sampled twice and replayed. Cycles are per warp. Two corrections to the method, found in the data: (1) one stall sample is taken per SM and interval whatever the number of resident warps, so sample shares between classes are not residency shares; a class's samples are scaled with that class's own counter (derive.py), which is what the numbers below use. (2) The h100 metric list lacked the `wait` counter (taken over from the full-GPU list); it is added now, and h100 `wait` values of this run exist only as clock differences. Sampling rows under 2000 samples: 36 on h100 (1000-1990 except the one-CTA shape), 4 on b300; they are used with their two passes shown, the one-CTA shape (10 / 30 samples) only for counters.

stall: W1 holds on both devices by the clocks: time per NOP = stall for stall 2..15 with either yield bit (2.03, 3.05, 4.03, 8.03, 11.03, 12.03, 15.03); stall 1 with yield bit 1 is 1.03 when the code is resident (launch 2, and at 32 warps per CTA) and 1.5-1.8 on a cold launch (the difference is no_instruction; one b300 pass of the base shape reads 7.3); yield bit 0 with stall 1 costs 2.05 (class misc), with stall 0 costs 33.4 per NOP (class wait). b300 samples: wait per NOP = stall - 1 within 0.1 for every stall, share of the non-selected samples at least 0.99. With 8 warps per SMSP and stall 1 a warp's 64 NOPs take 1.03-1.06 each: the warp keeps the issue slot while it is ready (the others are not_selected); with stall 4, 5.2 (b300) / 5.6 (h100) per NOP. The replay gives 5.58 per NOP at stall 1 on b300 (issue_slot 4.5) and 8.3 / 7.9 at stall 4. barrier_visibility: V1 on both devices: only s1.g0 has wrong values (every thread). fixed_latency (`VIADD R5, R5, 0x1` in place, 64 times): stall 1 and 2: every thread ends with +32 or +33; stall 3: one add lost in 128 of 33792 threads (h100) / in half of the threads (b300); stall 4: all right. So the hardware never holds the reader of a fixed-latency result: it computes with the old value. Clock per add: 3.9 at stall 1 and 2, 4.03, 4.05 on a cold launch; at launch 2: 2.98 / 2.99 (h100), 2.02 / 2.03 (b300). Samples at stall 1: math_pipe_throttle 1.6-1.8 per add and not_selected 0.6. Reading (inference): the pipe takes one such add of a SMSP every 2 cycles; two warps of a SMSP that reach the chain together get 3.9 each. A one-warp-per-SMSP shape of d.add was not among the cells; it goes to the next version. The replay holds the reader on the register instead (reg:VIADD 3.9 per add at stall 1 on h100) and gives 1.55 per add on b300.

addenda.when: same runs — start, exit, code fetch (a, b)
addenda.text: exit_drain: E1 on both devices. Drain after EXIT: no stack load (a.exit_only, a.nop_exit) 6-8; a.empty 97 (h100) / 107 (b300); with 16 NOPs between the stack load and EXIT 70 / 69; with 64 or 256 NOPs 5-7; sleds of 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 lines 88 / 77 / 42 / 7 (h100), 106 / 97 / 42 / 5 (b300). The drain is the rest of the stack LDC's first-touch latency (about 100 cycles from its issue); the fixed part after EXIT is branch_resolving 8 + wait 4-6 + drain 5-8. first_instruction (no_instruction on the first pc): F1 on both devices: flat in warps per CTA and CTAs per SM as long as they start together, and with 16 CTAs per SM (waves) the mean falls to 80 (h100) / 238 (b300) while 0.77 of the warps' stack-load requests hit. Levels: h100 is between 205 and 340 in most cells (a.nop_exit 240, a.empty.w1 227, a.empty.g4 206, sleds of 1..32 lines 249-273, 128 lines 325, one CTA 213) and at 400-460 in a.empty (443) and a.exit_only (436), both passes agreeing within 20, and in single passes of three cells (a.empty.w32 253 / 418, a.stack_nop64_exit 400 / 254, b.sled.l64 459 / 339). The level does not follow the kernel's content; unexplained. b300: 530-590 in most cells, single passes at 640-1020 (a.empty.w32 913 / 1019, a.empty.g4 866 / 534, a.stack_nop64_exit 948 / 834, b.sled.l16 534 / 822), one CTA 728. SM active cycles of a.empty (max / mean / min over SMs): h100 479 / 397 / 322, b300 894 / 688 / 498; replay 1209 and 344. fetch: after line 0, no_instruction per 128 B line is 6-10 (h100) / 9-15 (b300) with one or two larger lines early (h100 line 5: 42-59; b300 line 2: 16-44 and line 5: 38-72). Per additional line from 8 to 128 lines: SM active cycles (mean over SMs) 20.9 (h100) / 19.8 (b300), i.e. 8 issue cycles, about 9-10 of no_instruction and about 2 of not_selected at two warps per SMSP; replay 19.0 / 18.0 per line. The replay's error is the intercept: one-line sled 1209 against 396 mean / 474 max (h100), 350 against 697 / 892 (b300). b300 counters: requests of the per-GPC cache to L2 for instructions = 72 + 4.0 per code line (584 at 128 lines) with 8 sectors each: every GPC cache fetches the code in 256 B units; its instruction requests from the SMs are about 0.5 per line and SM; a function with 512 never-executed lines behind the kernel draws 1904-2036 of these L2 requests (the whole function is 259 units x 8 caches = 2072): the sequential fetch runs on through code that is never executed. h100's ncu has no counters for these levels; idc__requests there (and on b300) counts one request per LDC (1 per warp for the stack load), not instruction fetches.

Where the wait is: h100 uniform path (ULDC) at the load itself as imc_miss (share of load + reader over 0.95), b300 uniform path (LDCU) and the vector path (LDC) on both devices at the reader as short_scoreboard. First touch of a bank-0 line (pair cells, 8 warps per CTA): h100 ULDC 119-143, LDC 101-107; b300 LDCU 66-72, LDC 91-101. Another word of a loaded line: h100 ULDC 1-4, LDC 24-28; b300 LDCU 18-20, LDC 25-30. By warps per CTA (1 / 8 / 32): h100 ULDC 54-57 / 119-143 / 95-189 (with no_instruction next to it at 32), LDC 81-86 / 101-107 / 96-142; b300 LDCU 68-72 / 66-72 / 40-73, LDC 104-115 / 91-101 / 99-125. Batches: h100 ULDC loads hold one after the other whatever the order (4 loads 463, 8 loads 1037); the others are neither C1 nor C2: the first reader waits for the whole batch, h100 LDC 4 loads 179, b300 LDCU 4 loads 115 and 8 loads 237 (plus mio_throttle 6-11 on loads 5-7), b300 LDC 4 loads about 160-200 with passes apart: a first line costs the full latency and each further line of the batch about 15-30 more. Other path (S2 on both devices): a line loaded through one path costs a full first touch through the other (h100: LDC after ULDC 99-108, ULDC after LDC 79-131; b300: LDC after LDCU 97-103, LDCU after LDC 65-69). Counters agree: idc__requests counts the LDCs only (3 per warp in the uniform cells, 11 in the vector cells; the re-reads are its hits), b300's sm__dcc_requests counts the LDCUs only. Bank 3: the first line of each 256 B block costs 552-714 (h100 ULDC), 630-720 (h100 LDC), 635-672 (b300 LDCU), 629-841 (b300 LDC); the other lines of a block cost what a bank-0 line costs. b300 counters: bank-0 requests to the per-GPC cache never miss in the late-position cells (the parameter bank is there at launch), the bank-3 cells miss 3 times per SM and send 24 requests to L2 (3 blocks x 8 caches). Position (T): as the kernel's first instructions the loads cost about the same as late (h100 ULDC 108-172 against 119-143; b300 first reader 122, second 93, then 68-73). Code size (T2 on both devices): with 512 never-executed code lines behind the kernel the first head loads cost h100 450 / 202 / 151 and then 125-139, b300 392 / 108 and then 74-80; in late position the first three cost 140-177 (h100), unchanged on b300; b300's per-GPC cache then misses 156-234 of its constant requests (0-33 without the tail). This reproduces in kind what the full-GPU reference shows on the first constant loads of real kernels (ULDC about 310 against 126-150 on the earlier probes): the first constant loads of a large kernel wait while the code fetch is using the same path. Replay against these: h100 ULDC first touch 130.5 at every shape (hardware 55 at one warp per SM), LDC reader 150 (hardware about 103), bank-3 uniform 232 per line (hardware 130 / 550-710 by position in the block), one resident set for both paths (hardware: two); b300 LDCU reader about 500 (hardware 70), LDC reader 28 on first touch (hardware about 95).

Nothing is installed from this version. The next versions, each with its engine rule declared before its data: (1) constant reads: two resident sets per SM (uniform path / LDC path), first-touch and re-read latencies per path and device, the 256 B block cost of banks behind the per-GPC cache, pipelined service of a batch, and the one-warp-per-SM level of the h100 uniform path; (2) kernel start and exit: the wait before the first instruction as the cold fetch of the first code line (shared by the SM's warps, absent for later waves) and the exit drain as the completion of outstanding variable-latency instructions, in place of the fitted lifecycle envelope; the two levels on h100 and the unstable b300 passes need their own cells (same kernel repeated, code address recorded); (3) code fetch: per-line cost and the early larger lines, the per-GPC 256 B unit, and the interaction with constant requests at the head of large kernels; (4) issue: the warp that issued keeps the slot while ready, the fixed-latency reader is never held on a register (only stall and barriers), one add per 2 cycles and SMSP (to be measured at one warp per SMSP and for the other classes).
